shloka_text: अथ रात्र्यां प्रवृत्तायां शत्रुघ्नो भृगुनन्दनम् । पप्रच्छ च्यवनं विप्रं लवणस्य यथा बलम् ।। 7.67.1 ।।
transliteration: atha rātryāṃ pravṛttāyāṃ śatrughno bhṛgunandanam | papraccha cyavanaṃ vipraṃ lavaṇasya yathā balam || 7.67.1 ||
translation: अथ then, रात्र्यां the night, प्रवृत्तायां having advanced, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, भृगुनन्दनम् the son of Bhrigu, पप्रच्छ he asked, च्यवनं Chyavana, विप्रं the brahmin, लवणस्य of Lavana, यथा how, बलम् the strength.
explanation: Then, as the night advanced, Shatrughna asked the brahmin Chyavana, the son of Bhrigu, about the extent of Lavana's strength.
comments: Shatrughna asks of the trident's power, and Chyavana tells of King Mandhata, who, having conquered the earth, sought heaven, but was told by Indra he must first subdue Lavana -- challenging the demon, Mandhata was burned to ashes with the trident -- Chyavana assures Shatrughna of victory on the morrow if he catches Lavana away from his weapon.

shloka_text: शूलस्य च बलं ब्रह्मन्के च पूर्वं विनाशिताः । अनेन शूलमुख्येन द्वन्द्वयुद्धमुपागताः ।। 7.67.2 ।।
transliteration: śūlasya ca balaṃ brahmanke ca pūrvaṃ vināśitāḥ | anena śūlamukhyena dvandvayuddhamupāgatāḥ || 7.67.2 ||
translation: शूलस्य of the trident, च and, बलं the strength, ब्रह्मन् O Brahmana, के who, च and, पूर्वं previously, विनाशिताः were destroyed, अनेन by this, शूलमुख्येन by the chief trident, द्वन्द्वयुद्धम् single combat, उपागताः who engaged in.
explanation: O Brahmana, Shatrughna further inquired about the strength of the trident and who had previously been destroyed by this formidable trident when they engaged in single combat.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः । प्रत्युवाच महातेजाश्च्यवनो रघुनन्दनम् ।। 7.67.3 ।।
transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā śatrughnasya mahātmanaḥ | pratyuvāca mahātejāścyavano raghunandanam || 7.67.3 ||
translation: तस्य his, तत् वचनम् that word, श्रुत्वा having heard, शत्रुघ्नस्य of Shatrughna, महात्मनः the great-souled, प्रत्युवाच replied, महातेजाः the greatly effulgent, च्यवनः Chyavana, रघुनन्दनम् to the delight of Raghu's lineage.
explanation: Having heard those words of the great-souled Shatrughna, the greatly effulgent Chyavana replied to the scion of Raghu.

shloka_text: असङ्ख्येयानि कर्माणि यान्यस्य रघुनन्दन । इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवे यद्वृत्तं तच्छृणष्व मे ।। 7.67.4 ।।
transliteration: asaṅkhyeyāni karmāṇi yānyasya raghunandana | ikṣvākuvaṃśaprabhave yadvṛttaṃ tacchṛṇaṣva me || 7.67.4 ||
translation: असङ्ख्येयानि innumerable, कर्माणि deeds, यानि which, अस्य of him, रघुनन्दन O delight of Raghu's lineage, इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवे born in the Ikshvaku lineage, यत् वृत्तम् what happened, तत् that, शृणष्व listen, मे from me.
explanation: O scion of Raghu, listen to me about the innumerable deeds and the story of him who was born in the Ikshvaku lineage.

shloka_text: अयोध्यायां पुरा राजा युवनाश्वसुतो बली । मान्धातेति स विख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु वीर्यवान् ।। 7.67.5 ।।
transliteration: ayodhyāyāṃ purā rājā yuvanāśvasuto balī | māndhāteti sa vikhyātastriṣu lokeṣu vīryavān || 7.67.5 ||
translation: अयोध्यायाम् in Ayodhya, पुरा formerly, राजा king, युवनाश्वसुतः son of Yuvanashva, बली powerful, मान्धाता इति as Mandhata, सः he, विख्यातः renowned, त्रिषु लोकेषु in the three worlds, वीर्यवान् valorous.
explanation: Formerly in Ayodhya, there was a powerful king, the son of Yuvanashva, who was renowned as Mandhata and was valorous in the three worlds.

shloka_text: स कृत्वा पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां शासने पृथिवीपतिः । सुरलोकमितो जेतुमुद्योगमकरोन्नृपः ।। 7.67.6 ।।
transliteration: sa kṛtvā pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ śāsane pṛthivīpatiḥ | suralokamito jetumudyogamakaronnṛpaḥ || 7.67.6 ||
translation: सः he, कृत्वा having made, पृथिवीम् the earth, कृत्स्नाम् entire, शासने under his rule, पृथिवीपतिः the lord of the earth, सुरलोकम् the world of gods, इतः from here, जेतुम् to conquer, उद्योगम् effort, अकरोत् made, नृपः the king.
explanation: Having brought the entire earth under his rule, that king, the lord of the earth, then made an effort to conquer the world of the gods from here.

shloka_text: इन्द्रस्य च भयं तीव्रं सुराणां च महात्मनाम् । मान्धातरि कृतोद्योगे देवलोकजिगीषया ।। 7.67.7 ।।
transliteration: indrasya ca bhayaṃ tīvraṃ surāṇāṃ ca mahātmanām | māndhātari kṛtodyoge devalokajigīṣayā || 7.67.7 ||
translation: इन्द्रस्य of Indra, च and, भयम् fear, तीव्रम् intense, सुराणाम् of the gods, च and, महात्मनाम् the great-souled, मान्धातरि when Mandhata, कृतोद्योगे had made the effort, देवलोकजिगीषया with the desire to conquer the world of gods.
explanation: Intense fear arose in Indra and the great-souled gods when Mandhata made the effort with the desire to conquer the world of the gods.

shloka_text: अर्धासनेन शक्रस्य राज्यार्धेन च पार्थिवः । वन्द्यमानः सुरगणैः प्रतिज्ञामध्यरोहत ।। 7.67.8 ।।
transliteration: ardhāsanena śakrasya rājyārdhena ca pārthivaḥ | vandyamānaḥ suragaṇaiḥ pratijñāmadhyarohata || 7.67.8 ||
translation: अर्धासनेन by half-seat, शक्रस्य of Indra, राज्यार्धेन by half-kingdom, च and, पार्थिवः the king, वन्द्यमानः being saluted, सुरगणैः by hosts of gods, प्रतिज्ञाम् a vow, अध्यरोहत he undertook.
explanation: The king, Mandhata, who was honored with half of Indra's seat and half of his kingdom, and saluted by the hosts of gods, then undertook a challenge.

shloka_text: तस्य पापमभिप्रायं विदित्वा पाकशासनः । सान्त्वपूर्वमिदं वाक्यमुवाच युवनाश्वजम् ।। 7.67.9 ।।
transliteration: tasya pāpamabhiprāyaṃ viditvā pākaśāsanaḥ | sāntvapūrvamidaṃ vākyamuvāca yuvanāśvajam || 7.67.9 ||
translation: तस्य his, पापम् sinful, अभिप्रायम् intention, विदित्वा having known, पाकशासनः Indra, सान्त्वपूर्वम् gentle, इदम् this, वाक्यम् word, उवाच he spoke, युवनाश्वजम् to the son of Yuvanashva.
explanation: Knowing Mandhata's sinful intention, Indra, the slayer of Paka, spoke these conciliatory words to the son of Yuvanashva.

shloka_text: राजा त्वं मानुषे लोके न तावत्पुरुषर्षभ । अकृत्वा पृथिवीं वश्यां देवराज्यमिहेच्छसि ।। 7.67.10 ।।
transliteration: rājā tvaṃ mānuṣe loke na tāvatpuruṣarṣabha | akṛtvā pṛthivīṃ vaśyāṃ devarājyamihecchasi || 7.67.10 ||
translation: राजा king, त्वम् you, मानुषे in the human, लोके world, न not, तावत् yet, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men, अकृत्वा without making, पृथिवीम् the earth, वश्याम् subservient, देवराज्यम् the kingdom of gods, इह here, इच्छसि you desire.
explanation: O best among men, you are a king in the human world, and you desire the kingdom of the gods here without first bringing the entire earth under your control.

shloka_text: यदि वीर समग्रा ते मेदिनी निखिला वशे । देवराज्यं कुरुष्वेह सभृत्यबलवाहनः ।। 7.67.11 ।।
transliteration: yadi vīra samagrā te medinī nikhilā vaśe | devarājyaṃ kuruṣveha sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ || 7.67.11 ||
translation: यदि if, वीर O hero, समग्रा complete, ते your, मेदिनी earth, निखिला whole, वशे under control, देवराज्यम् kingdom of gods, कुरुष्व do, इह here, सभृत्यबलवाहनः with servants, army, and vehicles.
explanation: O hero, if your entire earth is completely under your control, then you may establish the kingdom of the gods here with your servants, army, and vehicles.

shloka_text: इन्द्रमेवं ब्रुवाणं तं मान्धाता वाक्यमब्रवीत् । क्व मे शक्र प्रतिहतं शासनं पृथिवीतले ।। 7.67.12 ।।
transliteration: indramevaṃ bruvāṇaṃ taṃ māndhātā vākyamabravīt | kva me śakra pratihataṃ śāsanaṃ pṛthivītale || 7.67.12 ||
translation: इन्द्रम् to Indra, एवम् thus, ब्रुवाणम् speaking, तम् to him, मान्धाता Mandhata, वाक्यम् word, अब्रवीत् he spoke, क्व where, मे my, शक्र O Indra, प्रतिहतम् obstructed, शासनम् rule, पृथिवीतले on the surface of the earth.
explanation: To Indra, who was speaking thus, Mandhata replied, "O Indra, where on the surface of the earth is my rule obstructed?"

shloka_text: तमुवाच सहस्राक्षो लवणो नाम राक्षसः । मधुपुत्रो मधुवने न ते ऽ ऽज्ञां कुरुते ऽनघ ।। 7.67.13 ।।
transliteration: tamuvāca sahasrākṣo lavaṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ | madhuputro madhuvane na te ' 'jñāṃ kurute 'nagha || 7.67.13 ||
translation: तम् him, उवाच said, सहस्राक्षः Indra, लवणः Lavana, नाम named, राक्षसः demon, मधुपुत्रः son of Madhu, मधुवने in Madhuvana, न not, ते your, आज्ञाम् command, कुरुते obeys, अनघ O sinless one.
explanation: Indra informed (Shatrughna) that a demon named Lavana, son of Madhu, residing in Madhuvana, does not obey his commands, O sinless one.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा विप्रियं घोरं सहस्राक्षेण भाषितम् । व्रीडितो ऽवाङ्मुखो राजा व्याहर्तुं न शशाक ह ।। 7.67.14 ।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā vipriyaṃ ghoraṃ sahasrākṣeṇa bhāṣitam | vrīḍito 'vāṅmukho rājā vyāhartuṃ na śaśāka ha || 7.67.14 ||
translation: तत् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, विप्रियम् unpleasant, घोरम् terrible, सहस्राक्षेण by Indra, भाषितम् spoken, व्रीडितः ashamed, अवाङ्मुखः with downcast face, राजा the king, व्याहर्तुम् to speak, न not, शशाक was able, ह indeed.
explanation: Having heard those terrible and unpleasant words spoken by Indra, the king (Shatrughna) was ashamed and, with a downcast face, was indeed unable to speak.

shloka_text: आमन्त्र्य तु सहस्राक्षं ह्रिया किञ्चिदवाङ्मुखः । पुनरेवागमच्छ्रीमानिमं लोकं नरेश्वरः ।। 7.67.15 ।।
transliteration: āmantrya tu sahasrākṣaṃ hriyā kiñcidavāṅmukhaḥ | punarevāgamacchrīmānimaṃ lokaṃ nareśvaraḥ || 7.67.15 ||
translation: आमन्त्र्य having bid farewell, तु and, सहस्राक्षम् to Indra, ह्रिया with shame, किञ्चित् somewhat, अवाङ्मुखः with downcast face, पुनरेव again indeed, आगमत् came, श्रीमान् glorious, इमम् this, लोकम् world, नरेश्वरः the lord of men.
explanation: And having bid farewell to Indra, the glorious lord of men (Shatrughna), still somewhat ashamed and with a downcast face, returned to this world.

shloka_text: स कृत्वा हृदये ऽमर्षं सभृत्यबलवाहनः । आजगाम मधोः पुत्रं वशे कर्तुमरिन्दमः ।। 7.67.16 ।।
transliteration: sa kṛtvā hṛdaye 'marṣaṃ sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ | ājagāma madhoḥ putraṃ vaśe kartumarindamaḥ || 7.67.16 ||
translation: सः he, कृत्वा having placed, हृदये in his heart, अमर्षम् indignation, सभृत्यबलवाहनः with servants, army, and vehicles, आजगाम came, मधोः of Madhu, पुत्रम् the son, वशे under control, कर्तुम् to make, अरिन्दमः the subduer of enemies.
explanation: Holding indignation in his heart, the subduer of enemies (Shatrughna) came with his servants, army, and vehicles to bring Madhu's son (Lavana) under his control.

shloka_text: स काङ्क्षमाणो लवणं युद्धाय पुरुषर्षभः । दूतं सम्प्रेषयामास सकाशं लवणस्य हि ।। 7.67.17 ।।
transliteration: sa kāṅkṣamāṇo lavaṇaṃ yuddhāya puruṣarṣabhaḥ | dūtaṃ sampreṣayāmāsa sakāśaṃ lavaṇasya hi || 7.67.17 ||
translation: सः he, काङ्क्षमाणः desiring, लवणम् Lavana, युद्धाय for battle, पुरुषर्षभः the best among men, दूतम् a messenger, सम्प्रेषयामास sent, सकाशम् to the presence, लवणस्य of Lavana, हि indeed.
explanation: Desiring battle with Lavana, the best among men (Shatrughna) indeed sent a messenger to Lavana's presence.

shloka_text: स गत्वा विप्रियाण्याह बहूनि मधुनः सुतम् । वदन्तमेवं तं दूतं भक्षयामास राक्षसः ।। 7.67.18 ।।
transliteration: sa gatvā vipriyāṇyāha bahūni madhunaḥ sutam | vadantamevaṃ taṃ dūtaṃ bhakṣayāmāsa rākṣasaḥ || 7.67.18 ||
translation: सः he, गत्वा having gone, विप्रियाणि unpleasant things, आह said, बहूनि many, मधुनः of Madhu, सुतम् to the son, वदन्तम् speaking, एवम् thus, तम् that, दूतम् messenger, भक्षयामास devoured, राक्षसः the demon.
explanation: Having gone and spoken many unpleasant things to Madhu's son, the demon Lavaṇa devoured that messenger who was speaking thus.

shloka_text: चिरायमाणे दूते तु राजा क्रोधसमन्वितः । अर्दयामास तद्रक्षः शरवृष्ट्या समन्ततः ।। 7.67.19 ।।
transliteration: cirāyamāṇe dūte tu rājā krodhasamanvitaḥ | ardayāmāsa tadrakṣaḥ śaravṛṣṭyā samantataḥ || 7.67.19 ||
translation: चिरायमाणे when delaying, दूते the messenger, तु indeed, राजा the king, क्रोधसमन्वितः filled with anger, अर्दयामास tormented, तद्रक्षः that demon, शरवृष्ट्या with a shower of arrows, समन्ततः from all sides.
explanation: When the messenger delayed, the king, filled with anger, attacked that demon Lavaṇa from all sides with a shower of arrows.

shloka_text: ततः प्रहस्य तद्रक्षः शूलं जग्राह पाणिना । वधाय सानुबन्धस्य मुमोचायुधमुत्तमम् ।। 7.67.20 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ prahasya tadrakṣaḥ śūlaṃ jagrāha pāṇinā | vadhāya sānubandhasya mumocāyudhamuttamam || 7.67.20 ||
translation: ततः then, प्रहस्य having laughed loudly, तद्रक्षः that demon, शूलम् the trident, जग्राह took, पाणिना with his hand, वधाय for the killing, सानुबन्धस्य along with his retinue, मुमोच released, आयुधम् the weapon, उत्तमम् excellent.
explanation: Then, that demon Lavaṇa laughed loudly, took the excellent trident in his hand, and released that supreme weapon to kill the king along with his retinue.

shloka_text: तच्छूलं दीप्यमानं तु सभृत्यबलवाहनम् । भस्मीकृत्वा नृपं भूयो लवणस्यागमत्करम् ।। 7.67.21 ।।
transliteration: tacchūlaṃ dīpyamānaṃ tu sabhṛtyabalavāhanam | bhasmīkṛtvā nṛpaṃ bhūyo lavaṇasyāgamatkaram || 7.67.21 ||
translation: तत् that, शूलम् trident, दीप्यमानम् shining brightly, तु indeed, सभृत्यबलवाहनम् along with servants, army, and vehicles, भस्मीकृत्वा having reduced to ashes, नृपम् the king, भूयः again, लवणस्य of Lavaṇa, आगमत् returned, करम् to the hand.
explanation: That brightly shining trident, having reduced the king along with his servants, army, and vehicles to ashes, then returned to Lavaṇa's hand.

shloka_text: एवं स राजा सुमहान्हतः सबलवाहनः । शूलस्य तु बलं सौम्य अप्रमेयमनुत्तमम् ।। 7.67.22 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ sa rājā sumahānhataḥ sabalavāhanaḥ | śūlasya tu balaṃ saumya aprameyamanuttamam || 7.67.22 ||
translation: एवम् thus, सः that, राजा king, सुमहान् very great, हतः was killed, सबलवाहनः along with his army and vehicles, शूलस्य of the trident, तु indeed, बलम् the power, सौम्य O gentle one, अप्रमेयम् immeasurable, अनुत्तमम् unsurpassed.
explanation: Thus, that very great king was killed along with his army and vehicles; indeed, O gentle one, the power of that trident is immeasurable and unsurpassed.

shloka_text: श्वः प्रभाते तु लवणं वधिष्यसि न संशयः । अगृहीतायुधं क्षिप्रं ध्रुवो हि विजयस्तव ।। 7.67.23 ।।
transliteration: śvaḥ prabhāte tu lavaṇaṃ vadhiṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ | agṛhītāyudhaṃ kṣipraṃ dhruvo hi vijayastava || 7.67.23 ||
translation: श्वः tomorrow, प्रभाते in the morning, तु indeed, लवणं Lavana, वधिष्यसि you will kill, न not, संशयः doubt, अगृहीतायुधं when he has not taken his weapon, क्षिप्रं swiftly, ध्रुवो certain, हि indeed, विजयस्तव your victory.
explanation: Tomorrow morning, you will certainly kill Lavana, and your victory is assured, especially when he has not taken up his weapon.

shloka_text: लोकानां स्वस्ति चैव स्यात्कृते कर्मणि च त्वया । एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं लवणस्य दुरात्मनः ।। 7.67.24 ।।
transliteration: lokānāṃ svasti caiva syātkṛte karmaṇi ca tvayā | etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ lavaṇasya durātmanaḥ || 7.67.24 ||
translation: लोकानां for the people, स्वस्ति welfare, चैव and indeed, स्यात् will be, कृते when done, कर्मणि the deed, च and, त्वया by you, एतत् this, ते to you, सर्वम् all, आख्यातं has been told, लवणस्य of Lavana, दुरात्मनः the wicked one.
explanation: The welfare of the worlds will be achieved by this deed done by you, and all this about the wicked Lavana has been told to you.

shloka_text: शूलस्य च बलं घोरमप्रमेयं नरर्षभ । विनाशश्चैव मान्धातुर्यत्तेनाभूच्च पार्थिव ।। 7.67.25 ।।
transliteration: śūlasya ca balaṃ ghoramaprameyaṃ nararṣabha | vināśaścaiva māndhāturyattenābhūcca pārthiva || 7.67.25 ||
translation: शूलस्य of the trident, च and, बलं strength, घोरम् terrible, अप्रमेयं immeasurable, नरर्षभ O best among men, विनाशश्चैव and indeed the destruction, मान्धातुः of Mandhata, यत् which, तेन by him, अभूत् happened, च and, पार्थिव O king.
explanation: O best among men, the terrible and immeasurable strength of the trident, and the destruction of Mandhata which was caused by him, has also been recounted, O king.

shloka_text: त्वं श्वः प्रभाते लवणं महात्मन्वधिष्यसे नात्र तु संशयो मे । शूलं विना निर्गतमामिषार्थे ध्रुवो जयस्ते भविता नरेन्द्र ।। 7.67.26 ।।
transliteration: tvaṃ śvaḥ prabhāte lavaṇaṃ mahātmanvadhiṣyase nātra tu saṃśayo me | śūlaṃ vinā nirgatamāmiṣārthe dhruvo jayaste bhavitā narendra || 7.67.26 ||
translation: त्वं you, श्वः tomorrow, प्रभाते in the morning, लवणं Lavana, महात्मन् O great-souled one, वधिष्यसे you will kill, न not, अत्र here, तु indeed, संशयः doubt, मे my, शूलं the trident, विना without, निर्गतम् having gone out, आमिषार्थे for the sake of meat, ध्रुवो certain, जयस्ते your victory, भविता will be, नरेन्द्र O king.
explanation: O great-souled one, you will kill Lavana tomorrow morning; there is no doubt in my mind about this, and your victory will be certain, O king, when he has gone out without his trident for the sake of food. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 67 ।। Thus ends the sixty-seventh sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
